name: The DAO
loss_note: about 3.6M ETH, roughly $60M at the time
tldr: The first famous smart contract hack: a withdraw function sent ETH before updating the balance, so the attacker withdrew again and again.
what: The DAO was a community investment fund that lived entirely in a smart contract. People sent ETH in and got tokens that let them vote on projects.
happened: An attacker used a contract that, every time it received ETH, called the withdraw function again. The DAO kept paying because the balance was only updated at the end.
bug: Wrong order of steps: send money first, update the books later. That gap is where the attacker kept re-entering.
prevent: Update the balance before sending money (checks-effects-interactions) and add a reentrancy guard.
lesson: Whenever a contract talks to the outside world, assume the outside world can call back in. Ethereum later hard-forked to return the funds, which created Ethereum Classic.
